descriptionHtml:
112 × 84cm. Flannel on top. Their back covered and the door in view.

Esthwaite is an orthopaedic chaise dog bed, 112 × 84 × 15cm, with a layered foam base and an egg-crate upper profile. An L-shaped bolster runs along two sides and a soft flannel surface covers the sleeping area.

Plenty of dogs never settle in the bed you bought and sleep in the doorway instead. It is not the foam they are turning down. From a doorway they can see the hall, the stairs and you, and four walls take all of that away.

Two raised sides give them a corner to back into. The other two sit open at floor level, so the view down the room stays exactly where it was.

What they get

  • An L-shaped bolster: Cover along two sides and a corner to rest a chin in.
  • Two open sides: Nothing blocking the sightline and nothing to climb.
  • Layered foam with an egg-crate upper profile: A profiled surface that shares the weight across more of them.
  • Soft flannel where they lie: The sleeping surface runs across the whole open area.

Best for: watchful dogs who sleep facing the door, large dogs in the room the family uses, and anyone whose dog keeps choosing the hallway.

Why it is worth the money

£139 is a lot for a dog bed, so here is where it goes. Shape is the reason most beds get abandoned, not comfort. A watchful dog will not settle in a box however good the foam is. You are buying 112 × 84cm of usable floor with the walls only where they help, over a layered base with an egg-crate profile on top.

And you are not gambling the money. If they have not claimed it within 100 nights, we collect it free from the UK mainland and refund you in full.

Now the trade-off. At 15cm this is the shallower of the two chaise beds we make, and there is no waterproof lining in it. A dog at the very heavy end of large is better on 18cm, and a household with regular accidents wants one of the sofa beds with a liner.

Size and fit

SizeExternal (cm)Shape
One size112 × 84 × 15L-shaped bolster on two sides, two sides usable to the edge

Measure your dog lying on their side, nose to base of tail, and add 15 to 20cm. Not sure? Message us their breed and weight and we will tell you honestly whether it fits.

Everyday care

Follow the sewn-in care label on the cover. Air-dry it fully before refitting. Never wash or soak the foam.

If your dog is in pain, recovering or finding it hard to move, speak to your vet about the right resting surface. A bed is for comfort. It is not a treatment.

100 nights to decide

Try it at home for 100 nights from delivery. If it is not right, we arrange free UK mainland collection and a full refund. One trial per household; damage and other exclusions apply. Read the full returns and guarantee terms.

The questions we get asked most

Which two sides are open?

The bolster runs along two adjoining edges in an L. The remaining two are open right to the edge, so they can lie with their spine in the corner and their legs over the open side.

Is 15cm of foam enough for a big dog?

What we can describe is the build, not the outcome. It is a layered base with an egg-crate profile on top, across 112 × 84cm. Bowfell is the same shape at 18cm if yours is heavier.

Free standard UK delivery on orders over £40. Check delivery timings and any product-specific lead time.

Give them a corner to back into and keep the door in view.
